messages:
matt: quick thread — I'm sketching a proposal for how we map trace age to storage tiers + access SLAs. goal: keep common debug windows fast but stop paying for full retention hot. thoughts?
priya: +1 on the goal. can you share typical query patterns? e.g., do we need full-fidelity traces searchable after 30d?
matt: from recent dashboards: 95% of trace lookups are <14d, almost all are for prod. staging/dev lookups are mostly <3d. long tail is rare but expensive.
nada: small nit — call me ada :) cost is obvious but also keep in mind latency SLO for per-request span lookup (dashboard trace flyout). if we evict indexes too early UX suffers.
ezra: what about a tiered "warm" window per environment: dev 24h warm, staging 7d warm, prod 14-30d warm; after that move to compressed object store with async index rebuild on-demand?
priya: that async rebuild sounds risky for debugging incidents. can we have a cheap index (time-range + service) in cold store so we can at least locate traces without full scan?
matt: exactly what I was thinking — small shardable index in our column store (ClickHouse) for lookups, then fetch full spans from object store when needed. keep hot storage only for hot window.
astorage-bot: storage metrics: estimated monthly cost reduction 34% if prod warm=21d and cold archive afterwards. Query tail latency for archived-on-demand could be 10s-30s depending on IO.
ada: should we also consider sampled longer retention? e.g., keep 1% of traces at full fidelity for 1 year for long-term analysis / regressions?
ezra: yes. sample by error-rate + important-services. store sampled full-fidelity in a 'slow' bucket with separate access controls. makes audits possible without full cost.
priya: operational: need a clear rollout plan and a console UI showing which traces are warm vs archived (so SREs know why a trace might be slow). also add quota guardrails for on-demand rehydrate.
matt: draft config sketch: `{
  "environments": {
    "dev": {"warm_days": 1, "cold_tier": "object", "sample_rate_longterm": 0.0},
    "staging": {"warm_days": 7, "cold_tier": "object", "sample_rate_longterm": 0.01},
    "prod": {"warm_days": 21, "cold_tier": "object", "sample_rate_longterm": 0.01}
  },
  "indexing": {"min_index_fields": ["ts_bucket","service","trace_id"], "cold_fast_index": true}
}`
priya: love the config, but add a per-service override and an emergency keep-alive toggle for active incidents.
nada: +1 on override. also document OTLP exporter changes — we might want to add a span size header to pick heavy traces for immediate hot retention.
ezra: and unify exporter -> collector sampling hints so SDKs can mark traces as "must-keep" for 24h (useful during deploys).
matt: action items: I'll iterate config, add per-service override, produce a rollout playbook with feature flag + console indicators, and run a cost simulation. tagging @sre for review. thanks all :thumbsup:
priya: ok thanks — can you drop the sketch in #eng-platform-docs and add a tiny proto for the exporter hint?
matt: will do in next hour.
